description: C12 proposes a radically new approach to quantum hardware. Instead of scaling imperfect qubits (the basic units of quantum computers) and trying to compensate in the architecture, C12 uses material innovation to develop near-perfect building blocks first. It proposes ultrapure carbon nanotubes to trap single electrons which act as near-perfect spin qubits. C12 has the unique ability to manufacture these carbon nanotubes with the right dimensions and place them on a semiconductor chip. This approach and the purity of the material render the proposed hardware much more scalable than currently existing quantum computers, with drastically reduced error rates. Therefore, this novel approach could disrupt the nascent quantum hardware market which is poised to grow to a trillion-dollar industry in the coming years.
tagline: C12 develops quantum processors based on carbon nanotubes

description: Case45 has developed an AI prognostication model that considers cancer ecology which measures a patient’s immune response to the tumor. The company relies on digital images of histology slides, which are standard for diagnosing cancer. It works with any type of lab machinery. Case45 will analyze the data (a typical slide will have more than 1 million cells of different types present) and return the results to the clinic in minutes. The algorithm considers various factors by identifying and counting different cell types and their spatial relations. One crucial element is the analysis of immune infiltration—how many immune cells are present in the tumor and adjacent to it? (Tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes or TIL). Furthermore, the algorithm can detect the evolution history of the cancer by identifying “hot” and “cold” areas that are less or more infiltrated by immune cells.
tagline: Case45 predicts cancer's next move

description: DRAM and SRAM are the two most widely used memory technologies today. They are omnipresent in all electronic devices from data centers to laptops, mobile phones, and cars. Ferroelectric Memory Company (FMC) was established in 2016 in Germany. It has developed a disruptive technology that uses a patented new material to offer a new type of memory: Ferroelectric Non-Volatile Random Access Memory (Fe-NVRAM). As fast as DRAM, but non-volatile, Fe-NVRAM retains data even when disconnected from power. This reduces energy consumption by 90%.

description: Kandou AI is a Swiss hardware company developing copper-based interconnects for high-performance computing. It has three product lines focused on within-package interconnects, out-of-package interconnects and electronic packet switches. Kandou AI recently underwent a large restructuring and pivot into AI interconnects, and is raising a growth round. The demand for longer, ultra-high-bandwidth interconnects is driving two paths: integrating photonics closer to the chip despite high costs, or extending the current copper standard. Kandou AI is pursuing the latter with its core Chord signaling technology. Unlike standard differential signaling (1 bit over 2 wires), Chord signaling transmits a group of bits as a single mathematical unit (e.g., 5 bits over 6 wires). This results in correlated signals that reduce noise, increase bandwidth, and lower power consumption, forming the basis of their Copper MIMO (Multiple Input, Multiple Output) technology.
tagline: Kandou is developing high-speed energy-efficient chip-to-chip link solutions

description: Ncodin is a French deep-tech company revolutionizing the semiconductor industry with its breakthrough optical interconnect technology. As traditional copper connections hit their physical limits, Ncodin’s solution, built on the world’s smallest laser integrated on silicon, shatters these barriers. The company’s plug-and-play optical interposer enables unprecedented data transfer speeds and energy efficiency within next-generation processors. This allows chipmakers to overcome the end of Moore’s Law and unlock the full potential of AI and High-Performance Computing (HPC). Backed by leading European deep-tech investors and founded on over 15 years of pioneering research, Ncodin is paving the way for the future of computation.
tagline: Ncodin illuminates the future of computing

description: Neo Medical has developed a Swiss-made toolset for spine surgery. Its ease of use has convinced surgeons. It reduces complexity, operating time, and the risk of infections. Instead of several hundred parts, it uses five instruments and fourteen implants only, and it still does a better job, potentially reducing risks of screw loosening, hardware failure, and eventually further reducing re-operation risks, while improving overall patient outcomes. To enhance safety, Neo’s screws and implants are sterile and single-use, which removes the need for sterilization in the hospital. This reduces the environmental footprint of spinal fusion surgery by 75% versus legacy reusable systems.
tagline: Neo Medical makes simpler tools for spine surgery

description: neustark was founded in 2019 by Johannes Tiefenthaler and Valentin Gutknecht as an ETH Zurich spin-off. The two young entrepreneurs came together based on their shared vision of a solution for the utilization and storage of CO₂. In 2020, neustark’s first pilot plant was integrated into the production line of an established concrete producer. Today, various concrete producers store CO₂ with one of neustark’s mobile plants and produce concrete that is used both in private and public construction projects.
tagline: Neustark permanently stores CO2 in concrete

description: Once uses a “slow dating” approach. Users have 24 hours to get in touch with a single daily match, generated by their state-of-the-art artificial intelligence technology.
tagline: Once delivers one match per day

description: “EPFL spin-off ONWARD is helping paralysed spinal cord injury patients regain important functions, thanks to groundbreaking neurostimulation technologies. Based on world-leading research, impressive pre-clinical results and a network of key opinion leaders, ONWARD has developed two platforms that use the same principle. They electrically stimulate the patients’ nerves to re-establish body functions that will help patients lead a more independent and improved life. Tests have shown that ONWARD’s technology promotes neuroplasticity, i.e. the stimulation leads to an improvement in movement patterns even after it is turned off. ONWARD is working to enable patients to move again, for some this might mean regaining basic functions to feed or dress themselves, for others, it could even mean resuming complex tasks such as walking or playing the guitar.
tagline: Onward is empowering movement

description: Optalysys is a UK-based deep-technology company at the forefront of photonic computing. The company develops and commercializes optical co-processing accelerators that perform complex calculations at a fraction of the time and energy cost of traditional silicon-based systems. Designed for seamless integration into data centres and high-performance computing (HPC) environments, Optalysys’s technology is unlocking new frontiers in computationally intensive fields. A primary focus is making Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) commercially viable, enabling secure, privacy-preserving computation on sensitive data for the finance, healthcare, and cybersecurity sectors. By delivering a step-change in processing capability, Optalysys is providing the critical infrastructure for the next generation of artificial intelligence and secure cloud computing.
tagline: Optalysis enables the future of data security

description: Orakl Oncology is a French biotechnology company at the forefront of precision oncology. The company has developed a proprietary platform that leverages patient-derived organoids, or “tumor avatars,” combined with advanced artificial intelligence to predict patient response to cancer treatments. By creating one of the largest and most diverse living tumor biobanks, Orakl provides deep, biologically relevant insights into drug efficacy. This empowers pharmaceutical and biotech partners to de-risk and accelerate their drug development pipelines, improve clinical trial design, and ultimately bring more effective, personalized therapies to the patients who need them most.
tagline: Orakl Oncology accelerates drug discovery in oncology

description: Founded in 2015, Orbex is a UK-based orbital launch services company, serving the needs of the small satellite industry. The company has developed a microlauncher rocket that will be able to deliver 200kg of payload to orbit. The rocket uses 100% renewable fuel with 0% black carbon emissions and is largely reusable. Orbex designs and manufactures the whole rocket in-house and is also building its own dedicated launch site in Sutherland, Scotland. The Orbex team is highly experienced in the space industry, with their CTO, Jonas Bjarnoe, having worked on over 50 successful space missions for NASA, the European Space Agency (ESA) and the Danish space agency. Orbex is on track to become the first successful European microlauncher provider. The company is planning to launch its first rocket in 2023.
tagline: Orbex is enabling sustainable access to space

description: Orca Computing is a University of Oxford spin-off. It is developing quantum computing hardware based on light particles (photonics). Photonic quantum computers have some clear advantages. They use mostly existing telecom components for example and can run at room temperature without extensive infrastructure requirements. Furthermore, photons do not interact with the environment and are therefore much less sensitive to noise compared to other types of qubits. At the core of Orca’s technology is a patented quantum memory that allows it to trap and release photons on demand. This core innovation could be the answer to the fundamental challenge of optical quantum computing and therefore enable high-quality, scalable machines for a wide range of purposes.
tagline: Orca Computing is developing scalable photonic quantum computing

description: Otoqi is a startup that solves two distinct problems with the same IT platform: handling the management of shared car fleets and delivering newly bought or leased vehicles to clients. With a first-mover advantage, Otoqi is in a unique position to build the leading automotive e-logistics platform in Europe. For more than 11 European car-sharing companies, Otoqi provides the backbone that handles all the mundane tasks such as car repositioning, servicing, refueling, recharging and cleaning. For car manufacturers such as BMW, Volvo and Daimler and leasing companies, it delivers cars from logistics hubs directly to the clients. This service allows bypassing car dealerships as pickup points. It is essential for brands that want to increase their share of online car sales.
tagline: Otoqi is the provider of choice for carsharing firms

description: Identifying which bacteria or viruses have caused an infection is not straightforward with current methods. It takes several tests and several days, which in the context of hospitalized patients means it’s both expensive and slow. PathoQuest enables screening for more than 1200 pathogens with a single test instead of several. Patented blood sample preparation combined with bioinformatic processing and matching of results against a proprietary database make this breakthrough in diagnostics possible. PathoQuest’s CE-marked test significantly reduces the problematic use of broad-spectrum antibiotics. It is the major cause of antibiotic resistance, a growing danger to public health. PathoQuest scientific base is research by Prof. Marc Eloit, a world-leading virologist at Pasteur Institute in Paris.
tagline: PathoQuest modernizes diagnosis of infectious diseases

description: Phlair is developing a pioneering electrochemical direct air capture system. It removes CO2 from ambient air and industrial plants. Using standard components and patented technology, it uses less energy than competitors, which ultimately promises to lower costs to below USD 100 per ton. The process is also ideally suited to be combined with intermittent renewable energy sources such as wind and solar. Since its closed-loop mechanism splits a liquid into strong acids and basic solvents, these liquids can be stored as chemical energy storage. This means that the process can be powered by renewable electricity when available and cheap, unlike other DAC systems, which need constant electricity input.
tagline: Phlair enables next generation direct air capture

description: Chronic wounds are a widespread, growing phenomenon caused by an aging population and an increasing occurrence of diabetes. Wound care is an extremely large burden to healthcare systems, and has a huge impact on patients’ health and mental well-being. Direct medical cost, which includes treating wounds 2-3 times per week for months or years, is estimated to amount to up to USD 100 billion annually. The Swiss startup Piomic has developed an already CE-marked medical device that has been proven to promote the healing of chronic wounds that are difficult to treat and cause persistent pain to patients. Piomic’s COMS technology synergistically applies optical and magnetic stimulation externally to a wound. Its efficacy has been demonstrated in a clinical trial which showed a 2.5x accelerated wound healing rate. Piomic solution is the only one designed for home care and is highly cost-effective.
tagline: Piomic is developing an innovative device for wound care

description: Poppins has developed a breakthrough therapy based on 25 years of functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) studies in neuropediatrics that uses Cognitive Music Therapy (CMT) to help children aged 7 to 11 struggling with these learning impairments. Designed as a fun mini game application, it has been proven to offer the equivalent of 1 year of normal neurological development for a child with learning impairments in just 2 months of use. Poppins’ solution also helps raise children’s self-confidence by automatically adjusting the level of the games based on their abilities. Levels remain challenging, but easy enough to pass without repeated failures.
tagline: Poppins offers a digital therapy for children with learning disabilities

description: Conventional interim analyses are highly inefficient at finding the actual moment in a clinical trial where failure is inescapable or success conclusive. This costs the pharma industry $15bn+ in waste and delays. Presentient solves this with its breakthrough BRAKES platform which runs 20+ automated interim analyses while eliminating operational bias.
tagline: presentient shortens the length and cost of clinical trials

description: The company has developed a novel platform technology that facilitates surface modification of a range of select substrates with tailored “PFAS-friendly” molecular groups. The result is a suite of adsorbent materials, exhibiting high selectivity towards diverse PFAS compounds adaptable for multiple applications. PFAS infiltration into groundwater requires a dedicated approach to enable effective remediation of polluted groundwater sites. Our adsorbents can be implemented easily, enabling retrofitting of existing assets if required. The highly selective PFAS adsorbent requires shorter Empty Bed Contact Times, leading to lower footprints and lower CAPEX. The flexibility of the solution enables application in diverse sites and scenarios.
tagline: Advanced PFAS Removal Solutions

description: Q.ANT is the photonic technology scale-up that emerged from TRUMPF’s R&D labs with deep knowledge in light generation, processing and detection. Since its founding as an independent startup in 2018, the company has been advancing and industrializing photonic and quantum technologies in computing and sensing, specialized in Native Computing and Native Sensing by Q.ANT, pushing the boundaries into new application areas and processes.
tagline: Q.ANT is developing optical processors for AI workloads

description: Qnami manufactures quantum sensors that are able to measure magnetic fields at the nanoscale. The manufacturing of these sensors out of synthetic diamond is Qnami’s core competence. The company is developing a complete system consisting of a microscope, its quantum sensor and software to interpret the data. In a first step, the system is aimed at research laboratories and semiconductor manufacturers, allowing them for the first time to measure components at a nanoscale level. In the long-term, the technology is aimed to become applicable for industries such as medical imaging or automotive.
tagline: Qnami pioneers quantum sensors

description: Salonkee is an all-in-one software solution for hair and beauty salons that includes scheduling appointments, point-of-sales software, loyalty programs, and payments. description: Scrona is transforming the semiconductor and electronics industries with its groundbreaking InkLogic™ printhead platform, which enables high-volume, sub-micron precision printing of circuits and components on virtually any 3D surface. This technology unlocks next-generation applications like AI interposers, advanced antennas, quantum dot microLEDs, and photonic devices. The platform’s unique, software-defined architecture provides unmatched versatility, making it compatible with nearly any liquid material for future-proof manufacturing. After unveiling the world’s first 128-nozzle InkLogic printhead at CES 2025, Scrona was named “Start-up of the Year” at the prestigious IEEE ECTC conference in June 2025. The company’s business model is based on partnering with capital equipment OEMs worldwide to integrate its printheads, which are consumable units that create a strong recurring revenue stream. As a venture-backed spin-out from ETH Zurich, its core electrohydrodynamic (EHD) technology is protected by numerous patents and holds the world record for printing the smallest full-color image ever created.

The system is able to create broadcast-quality videos in many different environments such as sport productions, conferences and remote television sets. description: Sizable Energy is revolutionizing long-duration energy storage by adapting proven pumped hydro technology for offshore deployment. The company’s system uses a subsea reservoir on the ocean floor and a second floating on the surface, pumping saturated sea salt brine between them to store and release energy. This innovative approach unlocks unprecedented scalability and bypasses the geographical and land-use constraints of traditional methods.
tagline: Sizable Energy enables offshore pumped hydro energy storage

description: Somagenetix is a biotech company about to enter the clinical stage with next-generation precision gene therapy. Co-founder Janine Reichenbach, chaired Professor for Somatic Gene Therapy at the University of Zurich, and her team, leverage 15 years of world-class scientific and clinical expertise to disrupt this market with a novel technology platform. Somagenetix has the potential to become a next-generation breakthrough technology and a global leader in the field of blood cell (phagocyte) disorders. Phagocytes that do not function or function falsely play a crucial role in more than 50 diseases, ranging from immunodeficiencies, neurodegenerative disorders to cancers. Somagenetix’s technology platform allows for cell-specific expression, i.e. activation of genes only in specific targets, in this case, phagocytes.
tagline: Somagenetix develops groundbreaking gene therapies

description: Sympatient is building a proprietary operating system that turns psychotherapy delivery into a scalable system. It integrates coordinated access, operational execution, and structured quality/data systems – embedded directly into everyday clinical work. The result: a replicable delivery model for regulated care that expands capacity without compromising therapeutic standards and enables measurable performance uplift per practice.
tagline: Sympatient delivers digital psychotherapy

description: Involving test users early in the design process is a key factor for companies to ensure that new products succeed in the market. However, it is expensive and time-consuming to recruit the right test users. With TestingTime, companies can order test users in less than 5 minutes and conduct user research 48 hours later–10 times faster than other solutions. TestingTime’s automated recruiting service integrates seamlessly into the product testing process. Several hundred companies including global firms such as UBS or Google have worked with TestingTime and recruited test users out of a pool of more than 500’000 individuals for usability tests, interviews, focus groups and online surveys.
tagline: TestingTime is the test user recruitment platform

description: Therapixel is a medical imaging startup. It has developed software that can easily detect, locate and characterize breast cancer on medical images using artificial intelligence. Their product, MammoScreen, is currently used as a reading aid by radiologists for tens of thousands of patients per month. Therapixel’s core technical asset is an algorithm trained on a dataset of over a million mammograms (x-ray pictures of breasts) labeled by trained radiologists. MammoScreen helps speed up the reading process by highlighting those cases that merit a closer look. It also reduces the frequency with which cancer cases are missed, which is very relevant for reducing the cost from malpractice litigation which is customary in the US. The software has received CE marking and FDA approval.
tagline: Therapixel is automating breast cancer screening

description: Currently, only 40% of EV batteries undergo some form of recycling, with the remaining 60% winding up in landfills. Existing recycling methods are highly inefficient and fail to recycle the black mass, which are the materials of the anode and cathode of the battery. tozero has developed a novel way of recycling Lithium-Ion Batteries (LiBs) based on the CTO’s ’s years of research and development experience at RWTH Aachen’s Institute for Process Metallurgy and Metal Recycling (IME). Through a proprietary process of hydrometallurgy or chemical leaching, tozero is able to recycle up to 97% of the Black Mass in LiBs and for the first time recover the valuable Lithium. After having conducted over 70 successful tests in a laboratory setting, tozero is now focusing on scaling its process, with the ambitious goal of building its first commercial size plant with a 30k tonnes capacity by 2030.
tagline: tozero is developing a novel way of recycling lithium-ion batteries

description: Turn Energy has developed a novel, efficient reactor to reduce the carbon footprint of heavy industry. It produces green methane, which is also called renewable natural gas (RNG) because it uses renewable energy. The process combines carbon dioxide (CO2) and hydrogen (H2) and produces RNG (methane, CH4) and water (H2O). Placed next to an industrial plant, this reactor effectively allows the plant to reduce the amount of carbon dioxide going into the atmosphere. Capturing CO2 and turning it into RNG which can then be used by the plant as source of energy again, this innovative technology allows for a circular production process.
tagline: Turn2X produces renewable natural gas plants

description: Undecimal Bio is a biotechnology company addressing the biggest bottleneck in genetic medicine: the inability to deliver RNA therapeutics (specifically siRNA) directly and efficiently to specific cells outside of the liver, where a delivery vehicle already exists, but where no other small molecule delivery vehicles have been discovered for the past 20 years. While delivery to the liver has already been solved, delivering these gene-silencing medicines is the next frontier.
tagline: Undecimal.Bio creates novel extra-hepatic siRNA-small molecule conjugates

description: Veesion uses artificial intelligence and machine learning to prevent shoplifting in stores. The Veesion software runs on already installed cameras and analyzes gestures to detect possible theft without using facial recognition, and alerting employees via messages in real-time. The software is up to 20 times less expensive and catches 3 to 5 times more thefts than a security guard.
tagline: Veesion automatically detects thefts in real-time

description: Verity is a Swiss-based robotics leader specializing in AI-powered autonomous indoor drone systems. Co-founded by Kiva Systems (exited to Amazon for $775million) pioneer Raffaello D’Andrea the ETH Zurich spin-off enables “zero-error warehouses” through fully autonomous, 24/7 inventory tracking for global giants like IKEA and Maersk.

description: Versantis is a spin-off from ETH Zurich, Switzerland, developing a versatile antidote, capable of removing diverse toxic agents from the organism. Today, hospitals have no measure to deal with the acute form of cirrhosis. Using known and safe substances, the ETH spin-off has developed micro-capsules that trap ammonia and other toxins inside them. They will be applied in a procedure that these patients undergo in the hospital anyway.

WeMaintain has convinced some of Europe’s largest real estate owners such as Allianz, Swiss Life and BNP Paribas.

description: ETH spin-off Wingtra is the leading manufacturer of professional VTOL (vertical take-off and landing) drones for mapping and surveying. Its WingtraOne drone is able to cover large areas (up to 400ha, corresponding to 570 soccer fields) in a single fully autonomous flight. This combination and the ability to take off from anywhere regardless of terrain make Wingtra’s drones the instrument of choice for large-scale surveying.

description: Founded in 2019, yuri enables research in microgravity for any industry. They develop fully automated micro-labs the size of a wallet and launch them in behalf of scientists around the world to the International Space Station (ISS), on orbital and suborbital spacecraft, on parabolic flights, and on drop towers. The unique environment of microgravity is especially valuable in the life sciences, as human tissue grows in three dimensions and drug discovery can be improved. The founders Maria, Christian, and Mark build on more than 30 years combined engineering experience in the space industry and have successfully brought 11 payloads to the ISS to date.
tagline: yuri enables research in microgravity for any industry

description: Accelerometers and gyroscopes are everywhere – in cars, phones, robots, drones and in almost every electronic device that moves. However, mass-produced positioning sensors are reaching their performance limits. Zero Point Motion develops a chipset that allows highly precise navigation for the next wave of automation in vehicles and industrial applications. It is based on optical instead of capacitive measurement and is up to 10’000 times more precise than current mass-produced inertial sensors. The photonic technology enables military-grade positioning, indoors and outdoors, independent of GPS for industrial and consumer products that need affordable components.
tagline: Zero Point Motion develops hardware solutions to enable positioning and timing
